defects.description: The rise from 6 to more than 20 billion tonnes is called 'almost doubled', but 20 is more than three times 6, not roughly double.
paraphrases: 6 to over 20 billion tonnes is more than a tripling, not a doubling.
'Almost doubled' understates the 6-to-20 increase (which is over 3x).
Going from 6 to more than 20 cannot be described as almost doubling.
defects.rationale: Correct phrasing 'almost quadrupled' (20/6 ~= 3.3). Findable from the 6 and 20 figures in the same passage, distinct.

defects.description: The US ~400 billion tonnes is called 'almost one-half' of the ~1,600 billion tonne historical total, but 400 / 1,600 is one-quarter, not one-half.
paraphrases: 400 out of 1,600 is a quarter, not a half.
The US share of the historical total is miscalculated (should be about one-quarter).
400 billion is one-quarter of 1,600 billion, not one-half.
defects.rationale: Correct phrasing 'almost one-quarter' (400/1600). Findable from the US and total figures, distinct.

defects.description: The US total (~400 billion) is said to be 'more than 3 times' China's ~270 billion tonnes, but 400 / 270 is about 1.5.
paraphrases: 400 divided by 270 is about 1.5, not more than 3.
The US-to-China ratio is overstated (it is roughly 1.5 times).
400 billion is only about 1.5 times 270 billion, not three times.
defects.rationale: Correct phrasing 'more than 1.5 times' (400/270). Findable from the US and China figures in the same sentence, distinct from the share defect.
